extracted.intended_audience: U.S. Patent Office examiners and applicants preparing reissue patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for preparing, filing, and examining U.S. reissue patent applications (drawings, reissue oath/declaration, fees, surrender of original patent, IDS, public notice, and examination procedures). Primarily MPEP guidance for examiners with requirements applicants must meet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of original patent drawings in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The drawings of the original patent may be used as the formal drawings for the reissue application, and new drawings need not be submitted, provided that no alteration whatsoever is made in the original patent drawings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant desires to use original drawings as formal drawings, file a letter requesting transfer of the drawings from the patent file along with the reissue application and still submit, upon filing, a copy of the original drawings or a copy of the printed drawings. The formal transfer of the original drawing to the reissue application should be made by the examining group only when the reissue application is ready for allowance (not prior to allowance) because the reissue application might become abandoned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on amending original patent drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments to the original patent drawings are not permitted; any change to the patent drawings must be by way of a new sheet of drawings with the amended figures identified as 'amended' and with added figures identified as 'new' for each sheet changed submitted in compliance with § 1.84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any request to physically change original drawing sheets should be denied. New sheets must identify changed figures as 'amended', added figures as 'new', and a deleted figure must be enclosed in brackets and identified as 'canceled'. Noncompliant sheets will not be entered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for requesting drawing changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a change to the drawings is desired, a sketch in permanent ink showing proposed changes in red, to become part of the record, must be filed for approval by the examiner and should be in a separate paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examiner should inspect the sketch for presence of new matter, conformance with the specification as to structure and numbering, and anything else that could result in refusal of the request. If approved, the examiner will require a formal copy of the drawing sheet(s) with the proper labeling ('amended','new','canceled') and placement in the file as directed (inserted after existing sheets or replace by canceling the old sheet face-down with an 'X'). If a drawing change request is not approved or a sheet not entered, examiner will inform applicant in the next Office action, setting forth reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration: statement of belief re defect and at least one error
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath or declaration must state that the applicant believes the original patent to be wholly or partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing, or by reason of the patentee claiming more or less than the patentee had the right to claim in the patent, stating at least one error being relied upon as the basis for reissue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable sample language is provided (e.g., 'Applicant believes the original patent to be partly inoperative or invalid by reason of a defective specification or drawing.'). If both grounds apply, include both statements. The oath/declaration must identify at least one specific error (a single word, phrase, or expression in the specification or an original claim is sufficient). It is not sufficient to make only a generic statement that the application is filed to correct errors or to merely reproduce claims with brackets/underlining without identifying a specific error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration: statement that errors arose without deceptive intent
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue oath or declaration must state that all errors being corrected in the reissue application up to the time of filing of the oath or declaration arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Simple language suffices (e.g., 'All errors which are being corrected in the present reissue application up to the time of filing of this declaration arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant.'). Examiner reviews only that the averment is present; examiner does not opine on whether deceptive intent actually existed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue oath/declaration: examiner must review sufficiency and compliance with 37 CFR 1.63
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of the sufficiency of the reissue oath/declaration must in each case be reviewed and decided personally by the primary examiner; the oath/declaration must also comply with the requirements of 37 CFR 1.63.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.63(b) requires statements that applicant has reviewed and understands the specification and claims (as amended by any amendment specifically referred to), believes the named inventors to be the original and first inventors of the claimed subject matter, and acknowledges the duty to disclose information material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 14.01.05 with appropriate form paragraphs 6.03–6.09) to indicate defects in compliance with 1.63.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and sufficiency of the 'at least one error' relied upon
rubrics_metrics.description: The oath/declaration must identify at least one error relied upon to support the reissue application; identification of a single word, phrase, or expression in the specification or an original claim suffices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is not necessary to explain how or when the error arose or was discovered; such statements will not be reviewed by the examiner. If the identified 'error' is not an appropriate error under 35 U.S.C. 251, the oath/declaration is defective and the examiner should indicate this. If multiple errors are identified and at least one is an appropriate reissue error, that one suffices to support reissue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental reissue oath/declaration: when required and content
rubrics_metrics.description: For any error corrected which is not covered by the original oath/declaration, applicant must submit a supplemental oath or declaration stating that every such error arose without any deceptive intention on the part of the applicant; supplemental oath/declaration required before allowance and may be submitted with any amendment prior to allowance or to overcome a rejection under 35 U.S.C. 251.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A supplemental oath/declaration is not needed where (A) an appropriate error was previously stated and is still being corrected, or (B) only non-251 trivial errors (spelling, grammar, typographical, editorial, clerical) are corrected. If correcting an error after allowance, the supplemental must accompany the requested correction. The supplemental must state any newly covered errors arose without deceptive intent; if prior oath failed to state an error, supplemental must state one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue filing fees: claim-count fee calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: The reissue applicant is permitted to present every claim that was issued in the original patent for the basic filing fee; filing or later presentation of each independent claim in excess of the number of independent claims in the original patent requires a fee; filing or later presentation of each claim (independent or dependent) in excess of 20 and in excess of the number of claims in the original patent requires a fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees for claims in reissue continued prosecution applications are calculated the same way. The Office provides Form PTO/SB/56 (Reissue Application Fee Transmittal Form) to assist in correct calculation of reissue filing fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fees do not change with filing reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing of a reissue application does not alter the schedule of payments of maintenance fees on the original patent; if maintenance fees have not been paid and the patent has expired, no reissue patent can be granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 35 U.S.C. 251 authorizes reissue only for the unexpired term of the original patent. Examiner should determine whether all required maintenance fees have been paid prior to conducting examination and again when preparing the reissue application for issue. PALM may be used to check maintenance fee history. If the maintenance-fee payment window has closed and fee was not paid, reissue should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 251 as expired; if time remains to pay, do not reject under 35 U.S.C. 251.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer to surrender original patent and submission of original or affidavit of loss
rubrics_metrics.description: The application for a reissue must be accompanied by an offer to surrender the original patent and the application should also be accompanied by the original patent, or if the original is lost or inaccessible, by an affidavit or declaration to that effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An examination on the merits may be made even if the offer or original is not received, but the examiner should require the surrender or affidavit/declaration in the first Office action; the original patent or affidavit of loss must be received before allowance. If reissue is refused, original patent will be returned upon request. Forms PTO/SB/53, PTO/SB/54, or PTO/SB/55 may be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim for foreign priority in reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A claim for the benefit of an earlier filing date in a foreign country under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) must be made in a reissue application, even if previously made in the application on which the original patent was granted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No additional certified copy of the foreign application is necessary. 37 CFR 1.63 requires the oath/declaration to identify the foreign application by (A) application number, (B) foreign country, and (C) day, month, and year of filing of the foreign application. Examiner should ensure the file wrapper is endorsed under 'FOREIGN APPLICATIONS' because the heading on printed copies of the patent will not be carried forward from the original patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure and Information Disclosure Statements in reissue
rubrics_metrics.description: A reissue application is subject to the same duty of disclosure as any other nonprovisional application; 37 CFR 1.63 requires acknowledgement in the reissue oath or declaration of the duty to disclose all information known to be material to patentability as defined in 37 CFR 1.56.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reissue applicants may use 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98 to comply with the duty of disclosure, but this does not remove requirements under 1.175 to state at least one error. Applicants are encouraged to file IDS at time of filing so statements will be available to the public during the 2-month period provided by 37 CFR 1.176. Use form paragraph 14.11.01 to remind applicant of continuing obligation to disclose litigation or other proceedings material to patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access, Official Gazette notice, and timing of examination
rubrics_metrics.description: All reissue applications filed after March 1, 1977 are open to inspection by the public and the filing of reissue applications (except CPAs filed under 37 CFR 1.53(d)) will be announced in the Official Gazette including specified identifying data; the announcement should be done prior to any examination of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Announcement gives the public opportunity to submit information pertinent to patentability. Examination of reissue should not occur sooner than two months after Gazette announcement. Office may postpone public access under appropriate circumstances to avoid interruption of examination. Requests for copies must be in writing to the Commissioner; copying fees per 37 CFR 1.19 apply. For reissue files filed prior to March 1, 1977, petitions for access are liberally granted by the Assistant Commissioner for Patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedures for reissue applications
rubrics_metrics.description: An original claim, if re-presented in the reissue application, is subject to reexamination, and the entire application will be examined in the same manner as original applications, subject to the rules relating thereto, excepting that division will not be required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications for reissue will be acted on by the examiner in advance of other applications, but not sooner than two months after announcement of the filing in the Official Gazette. Continued prosecution applications (CPAs) under 37 CFR 1.53(d) of a reissue application will not be announced in the Official Gazette; filing a CPA of a reissue is treated as filing a reissue but would be redundant to reannounce.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice placed in original patent file upon reissue filing and termination
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application for a reissue is filed, there will be placed in the file of the original patent a notice stating that an application for reissue has been filed; when the reissue is granted or the reissue application is otherwise terminated, the fact will be added to the notice in the file of the original patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.179. This notice tracks status of reissue filings in the original patent file.
